title: SYSK Selects: What happens in the brain during an orgasm?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun (originally from Christmas 2011) examining what happens in the brain during an orgasm. The hosts open with definitions of orgasm, then cover the nerve pathways involved (pudendal, pelvic, hypogastric and vagus nerves), the vagus nerve's role in paraplegic patients as described by Dr. Barry Komisaruk and Beverly Whipple's research at Rutgers, and the brain's reward circuit (ventral tegmental area, nucleus accumbens, pituitary release of endorphins, oxytocin and vasopressin). They discuss Dutch PET and fMRI studies comparing male and female brains (deactivation of the orbitofrontal cortex, changes in amygdala, hippocampus and insular cortex), orgasm disorders linked to SSRIs, persistent sexual arousal syndrome, orgasm in phantom limbs, a recent fMRI film of a woman's brain during orgasm, and theories on whether the female orgasm is an evolutionary byproduct. The episode closes with a listener mail about gene patenting and the Henrietta Lacks case.
rerun_of: What happens in the brain during an orgasm?

segments.title: Intro and framing the Selects episode
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode as a SYSK Selects pick from Christmas 2011 and discusses whether the show should cover sexuality as openly as violent topics. Chuck and Josh talk about parental discretion and sex ed.

segments.title: Definitions of orgasm
segments.summary: The hosts read definitions of orgasm from the Oxford English Dictionary, Merriam-Webster, and Alfred Kinsey, and discuss the comparison to sneezing and the myth that multiple sneezes equal an orgasm.

segments.title: Nerve endings and the genitalia
segments.summary: The hosts discuss nerve ending counts in the clitoris and penis, including a disputed claim about uncircumcised penises, and how the sensations travel to the brain.

segments.title: Pudendal, pelvic, hypogastric and vagus nerves
segments.summary: The hosts describe the major nerve bundles involved in orgasm. The vagus nerve bypasses the spinal cord and carries sensation directly to the brain, and it also plays a role in swallowing.

segments.title: Orgasm in people with spinal cord injuries
segments.summary: Komisaruk and Whipple's research at Rutgers found that women with severed spinal cords could feel cervical stimulation and reach orgasm, with fMRI showing vagus nerve brain activity. Hosts comment on the significance for paraplegic people.

segments.title: The brain's reward circuit and pleasure chemicals
segments.summary: The hosts explain the reward circuit, its discovery in 1950s rat experiments, and the roles of the nucleus accumbens, ventral tegmental area, amygdala, cerebellum, and pituitary gland. Endorphins, oxytocin and vasopressin are described, including their roles in bonding and childbirth.

segments.title: Dutch brain imaging studies: male vs female orgasm
segments.summary: Dutch researchers used PET and fMRI on people during orgasm. They found broad similarities, including orbitofrontal cortex deactivation in both sexes, and differences in regions such as the periaqueductal gray, amygdala, hippocampus, and insular cortex. Faked orgasms show a different brain pattern.

segments.title: Anorgasmia, SSRIs and persistent sexual arousal syndrome
segments.summary: The hosts discuss anorgasmia, the role of SSRIs in reducing dopamine and blocking orgasm, post-SSRI sexual dysfunction, and persistent sexual arousal syndrome, which Komisaruk studied with brain imaging. Meditation techniques are mentioned as a possible help.

segments.title: Orgasms from non-genital touch, imagery and phantom limbs
segments.summary: The hosts describe orgasms from nipple stimulation and from imagery alone, and orgasm felt in amputated limbs. They offer the cortical homunculus rewiring explanation while noting the uncertainty.

segments.title: Real-time fMRI film of a female orgasm
segments.summary: The hosts describe a newly released fMRI movie of a woman's brain approaching, experiencing and recovering from orgasm, including the study's helmet and practice methods, and the sequence of brain regions activated.

segments.title: Evolutionary purpose of the female orgasm
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why female orgasm exists, including the byproduct theory (comparing it to male nipples) and a twin study that did not support the byproduct explanation. They consider whether it is an evolutionary remnant.

segments.title: Listener mail: gene patenting and Henrietta Lacks
segments.summary: Jim from New Jersey writes that new genes can be patented but naturally occurring genes should not be. Josh and Chuck discuss how Henrietta Lacks' cells generated profits without her family receiving compensation.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and the producer, and give contact information and website details.
